newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline steady but unnerved by shut arb, crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline steady but unnerved by shut arb, crude.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices were steady in thin activity on Thursday, but traders warned the market was fragile after the arbitrage to the States closed and crude oil extended this week's selloff.
"The fundamental factor definitely is the arbitrage and whether it is open or not," said one Amsterdam trader.
"The sentiment in the States is bearish and for Europe the lifeline is the arbitrage," he said. "If it is going to open then Europe needs to come down a bit more."
NYMEX Feb gasoline lost 0.80 cent to 68.05 cents a gallon in overnight ACCESS activity and March lost nearly a cent to 68.35.
Eurograde barges traded at $217 fob a tonne for Rotterdam refinery material, but then bids were heard down to $214.50, and at $213.50 for Antwerp material, traders said.
ARA material was heard unchanged at $213/$215 but deals were scarce ahead of the NYMEX open and after this week's volatility in crude and gasoline.
Regular unleaded barges were assessed $10 lower at $203/$206 fob ARA, with no deals heard done.
Cash traders were also keying off the swaps where prices for the rest of January were up $4 at $216/$217, Feb gained as much to $217/$218 and March was traded at $220, up $2.
